review_notes:
I read the whole file. It has only two definitions, floatingCoordinates and floatingDegree. Neither duplicates a Mathlib concept. floatingCoordinates is a filter on the open interval (0,1) of a rational vector. floatingDegree counts the floating coordinates in the support of a 0/1 row. Both are specific to this argument, and I know of no Mathlib counterpart.

The other declarations are lemmas and theorems. Examples are exists_null_vector, which is a kernel-existence argument (a nonzero kernel vector exists when there are fewer equations than unknowns), and the double-counting lemma. Any overlap with Mathlib there is theorem or proof duplication, which the rubric excludes. The matrices are written as Fin m → Fin N → ℤ with explicit sums rather than Matrix.mulVec. I judged that a representation and style choice, not a competing concept, because the file defines no matrix or linear-map structure of its own. I found no clear case for consolidation, so I abstained. I did not run extensive searches of Mathlib. The remaining uncertainty is whether Mathlib has a named notion equivalent to the floating-coordinates set, and I consider that unlikely.
